summary: 7-phase plan (5.5h) for giving the inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint a pre/post baseline. Phase 1 adds an additive --findings mode to verify-deploy.sh emitting a normalized, sorted, deduplicated one-per-line findings set across all four gates plus a gate0 'could not run' sentinel; default-mode output and exit codes stay byte-for-byte unchanged. Phase 2 rewrites the authoritative Failure contract paragraph of the '### The Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint' subsection into three branches and resolves exit 2 explicitly. Phase 3 rewrites Stage MT-3 step 7 to capture a baseline immediately before deploy-headless.sh, diff it against the post-redeploy capture, and defer only on the set difference; deploy-headless.sh failure defers unconditionally with no baseline consultation. Phase 4 carries the new verify_deploy_baseline_notices ledger field through Stage MT-5 and the batch handoff without altering the exit-status resolution. Phase 5 renders the third operator-visible state with a loud banner, machine marker, and its own consolidated-output section. Phase 6 handles the out-of-scope skill-orchestrate-hard co-maintenance obligation by recording rather than silently expanding scope. Phase 7 sweeps all six verification-bar criteria.

artifacts.summary: 7-phase implementation plan with dependency waves, 8 recorded decisions, 3 scope notes, and per-phase verification tiers

decisions_made: Findings are emitted with a literal 'FINDING ' prefix and a gate0..gate4 label; the caller invokes 'verify-deploy.sh --findings --quiet' and filters with grep '^FINDING ' | sort -u. The prefix filter is load-bearing because the script's final PASS line is an unconditional stdout echo.

Exit 2 is folded into the ordinary findings vocabulary via one synthesized 'FINDING gate0 verify-deploy could not run: <reason>' sentinel rather than special-cased. Symmetric exit 2 (both runs) yields an empty difference and therefore the third state; asymmetric exit 2 (baseline established, post-redeploy unverifiable) yields a non-empty difference and defers.

Gate-3 findings include only 'FAIL:' lines, never 'ADVISORY:' -- narrows the research recommendation, because treating a new advisory as a newly-introduced finding would silently promote non-blocking advisories to blocking.

Finding text is normalized count-free before comparison (the STRICT_CORE_DEPLOY message's numeric count is dropped), so magnitude drift inside an already-failing check cannot manufacture a spurious 'new' finding. A genuinely redeploy-introduced instance still shows as absent->present.

The third state updates deployed_critical_paths exactly as the success path does -- the redeploy mechanically succeeded; without this the idempotence guard would re-fire the checkpoint every cycle purely because a pre-existing failure persists.

The third state gets its own mt_state_file field (verify_deploy_baseline_notices), never a defer_ledger entry, because defer_ledger's contract scopes it to defer/exclusion events and the third state excludes nothing.
The third state does NOT flip the batch exit status to 'partial'. Stage MT-5's three-branch resolution must not consult verify_deploy_baseline_notices.
The baseline is captured immediately before deploy-headless.sh, not earlier. When deploy-headless.sh then fails, the capture is discarded and the deferral is unconditional, consulting nothing.

Gate 3 captures its existing --quiet invocation (its FAIL detail survives --quiet); gate 4 re-invokes WITHOUT --quiet only in findings mode and only when that gate failed (its per-finding detail is suppressed by --quiet). This asymmetry is the one thing an implementer must get right.

skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md is NOT silently added to file_scope. Phase 6 records the co-maintenance divergence with exact replacement text unless an operator has already extended file_scope, in which case it mirrors the edit.
scope_notes: OUT OF DECLARED SCOPE: agent-system/extensions/core/skills/skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md carries a 'Transcribed: inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint' block under an explicit CO-MAINTENANCE contract ('an edit to either copy REQUIRES the same edit to the other'), and its failure sentence goes stale when Phase 3 lands. The file is not in this task's file_scope. Mitigating fact verified from skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's own mt_state_file schema block: skill-orchestrate-hard has NO MT-stage implementation of its own and uses the base multi-task stages, so the divergence is documentary, not behavioral. Phase 6 records it (or mirrors it if file_scope was already extended) rather than expanding scope.
The dependencies: [967] edge has no file-scope overlap with this task and is never referenced in this task's description; likely a batch-ordering artifact. No phase depends on it.

Three other not-yet-started tasks declare skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md in file_scope (one also declares commands/orchestrate.md). The admission gate never co-dispatches overlapping scopes, so no dependency edge is needed; an implementer should expect to rebase onto whichever lands first.
